data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella boat rental weather September 2037 trip? You're in luck: September is one of the best months to charter a boat on the Costa del Sol. With sea temperatures around 22°C, air temperatures between 25-30°C, and over 10 hours of daily sunshine, conditions are near-perfect for sailing, swimming, and exploring the coast. This guide covers what to expect, which boat to choose, and how to make the most of your day on the water from Puerto Banús.

September Weather in Marbella: What to Expect

September in Marbella is a transition month: summer heat lingers, but the intense peak-season crowds thin out. Average highs reach 28-30°C, with lows around 20°C. Sea surface temperatures are a pleasant 22°C, ideal for swimming without a wetsuit. Rainfall is sparse—typically less than 20mm for the month—and humidity is moderate. The sea breeze, often a light Poniente or Levante, keeps things comfortable. You can expect clear skies most days, with occasional afternoon clouds.

Best Boats for September Conditions

With calm seas and warm sun, any of our fleet works well. For groups up to 9, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m) is a reliable choice at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, including skipper, drinks, and IVA. The Azimut 39 (12.5m) offers similar value for up to 11 guests. If you want speed and style, the Mangusta 80 (24m) is a head-turner: from €4,719 for 4 hours, with a jet ski included free. For a more intimate trip, the Fairline Targa 12m (10 pax) or the Pershing 46 (10 pax) are excellent. All depart from Puerto Banús.

Ideal Itineraries for September

September's stable weather lets you plan longer trips. Head east from Puerto Banús towards Cabopino or Calahonda for quiet coves. Westwards, stop at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés for snorkelling. For a full-day adventure, cruise to Estepona or even Sotogrande—about 20-30 nautical miles each way. With an 8-hour charter on a Tier A boat, you can comfortably cover 60-80 NM and enjoy a long lunch at anchor. The skipper will adjust the route based on the day's wind and sea state.

What's Included in Your Charter

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Onboard, you'll find water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. That means no hidden costs—just show up with your swimwear and sunscreen. For larger yachts like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86, pricing is available on request via WhatsApp; our team will tailor a quote to your itinerary.

Booking Tips for September 2037

Mid-September is still part of the peak season, so book early—especially for weekends. The Mangusta 80 and Azimut 58 Flybridge are popular; reserve 2-3 weeks in advance. If you're flexible, weekday charters often have better availability. For the best value, consider a 4-hour morning trip (10:00-14:00) or an afternoon sunset cruise. Use our [boat rental Marbella](/blog/marbella-boat-rental-weather-september-2037-guide/) guide to compare options, or browse the full [fleet](/fleet/) to see what's available.

Safety and Weather Precautions

While September is generally calm, the Mediterranean can surprise. Our skippers monitor forecasts daily and will cancel or reschedule if winds exceed safe limits (typically above 25 knots). We recommend checking the forecast the day before your trip—look for wind speed and wave height. If you're prone to seasickness, choose a morning departure when seas are flattest. All our boats are equipped with life jackets and safety gear, and the skipper will brief you before departure.

What to Wear and Bring

Pack light: swimwear, a hat, polarized sunglasses, and a light cover-up for the breeze. Even in September, the sun is strong—bring SPF 50+ and reapply every 2 hours. A light jacket or sweater is useful for the return trip in the late afternoon. Don't forget a waterproof phone case and a towel. We provide all drinks and snacks, so you can travel light.
